subsections.title: The Essentials
subsections.summary: Six tools that protect most of your digital life.

items.title: A private browser
items.text: Your browser sees everything you do online. A private one blocks trackers, ads and fingerprinting by default, so websites and advertisers learn far less about you — without changing how you browse.

items.title: A private search engine
items.text: Searches reveal your health, money, plans and worries. A private search engine answers them without building a profile of you or tying them to your accounts.

items.title: A password manager
items.text: A unique, random password for every account, remembered for you. It stops one leaked password from unlocking the rest of your life, and it fills logins faster than typing.

items.title: An encrypted messenger
items.text: With end-to-end encryption only you and the person you’re talking to can read your messages and hear your calls — not the app maker, your carrier or anyone who breaks in.

items.title: A VPN you can trust
items.text: A VPN hides your browsing from your internet provider and public Wi-Fi, and swaps your IP address for its own. Choose an audited, no-logs provider — a bad VPN sees everything.

items.title: Encrypted storage
items.text: Keep photos, documents and backups where only you hold the key: an end-to-end encrypted cloud, or files encrypted on your own device before they’re uploaded.

blocks.after: Start with the first three — browser, search engine and password manager. Those three cover the widest surface for the least effort and make every other step easier.

subsections.title: Next Steps
subsections.summary: When the first three are done.

items.desc: A tick-off list of small fixes, from easiest to hardest.
Swap Google services for private ones, one at a time.
Add two-factor authentication to the accounts that matter most.
Find and remove the personal data already out there.
